message.content:
Below are two ways you can create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

---

## 1️⃣  `gcloud` CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Pick a zone that supports the RTX A6000 (e.g., us-central1-a)
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create a new instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
    --zone=$ZONE \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: your init script
```

> **Notes**
> * Replace `my-rtx-a6000` with your preferred instance name.
> * Adjust `--machine-type` if you need more or fewer CPUs/RAM.
> * The `--accelerator` flag attaches one RTX A6000 GPU.
> * Ensure you have the **NVIDIA GPU Driver** installed on the instance (you can add a startup script that installs the driver automatically).

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the REST API directly (or via Terraform / Pulumi), here’s a minimal JSON body you can POST to the Compute Engine Instances endpoint:

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "automaticRestart": true,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE"
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to POST this JSON

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace:
* `YOUR_PROJECT_ID` with your actual GCP project ID.
* `@instance.json` with the path to the file containing the JSON above.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Verify the zone (`us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, etc.) supports the RTX A6000. |
| ✅ | Ensure you have the **Compute Engine API** enabled in your project. |
| ✅ | Make sure you have the **NVIDIA GPU Driver** installed (via startup script or manual install). |
| ✅ | Check that your billing account is active and that you have enough quota for GPUs in the selected zone. |

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or add additional metadata/startup scripts as needed!
